comments.html:
Dear Editor and Reviewers,
We sincerely thank Reviewer A for the positive evaluation and constructive feedback, which helped improve the quality of our manuscript.
We have carefully addressed all the comments and revised the manuscript accordingly (changes are tracked/highlighted in the text):

  1. We have moderated our claims regarding the replacement of conventional AMI in the Conclusions section, stating it serves as a "cost-effective alternative or complementary solution".
  2. In the Results and Discussion section, we have added specific quantitative estimates regarding our experimental setup, end-to-end latency, engagement rates, and forecasting accuracy (MAPE) to address the concern about qualitative validation.
  3. We expanded the Data Persistence and Security section to explicitly mention data privacy measures, including TLS 1.3 encryption and pseudonymization.
  4. We attached the requested ZIP archive (Abstract_Bondarenko-20260916-fig.zip) containing the figure in high quality (fig01.png).

We believe these revisions fully address the reviewer's concerns and look forward to presenting our work at ETEME'26.

Best regards,
The Authors
comments.text:
Dear Editor and Reviewers,
We sincerely thank Reviewer A for the positive evaluation and constructive feedback, which helped improve the quality of our manuscript.
We have carefully addressed all the comments and revised the manuscript accordingly (changes are tracked/highlighted in the text):

1. We have moderated our claims regarding the replacement of conventional AMI in the Conclusions section, stating it serves as a "cost-effective alternative or complementary solution".
2. In the Results and Discussion section, we have added specific quantitative estimates regarding our experimental setup, end-to-end latency, engagement rates, and forecasting accuracy (MAPE) to address the concern about qualitative validation.
3. We expanded the Data Persistence and Security section to explicitly mention data privacy measures, including TLS 1.3 encryption and pseudonymization.
4. We attached the requested ZIP archive (Abstract_Bondarenko-20260916-fig.zip) containing the figure in high quality (fig01.png).

We believe these revisions fully address the reviewer's concerns and look forward to presenting our work at ETEME'26.

Best regards,
The Authors

revisions.judgment_comment:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer A:
The manuscript presents a practically oriented approach to behavioural demand response, combining a human-in-the-loop interface, low-code orchestration, predictive analytics, and automated consumer feedback. Its principal strengths are the originality of the proposed architecture, its potential for rapid and low-cost deployment, and its clear practical relevance to smart-grid applications. For these reasons, I recommend its acceptance for presentation.

revisions.judgment_comment:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer A:
The manuscript addresses an interesting topic, presenting a valuable applied case study in aluminum extrusion logistics. To further strengthen the paper, I have a few suggestions for the authors to consider. - On page 2 (first column, top), “(FEAL Web)” should follow the reference style required by the conference template if it is a reference. - In Section 3, several subsections lack clear formatting. I suggest adopting a consistent, numbered structure (e.g., 3.1 Organizational Adjustments) to make the text easier to follow. - The paper needs a clearer narrative thread. For example, on page 2 (second column), bullet points like “Separation of Technology and Planning” appear abruptly. A short introductory sentence would help readers understand how these points link to the preceding paragraph. Please check for similar situations. - Table captions and overall formatting do not match the conference template. - Figures 1 and 2 and Table 1 are central to the proposed model. Enhancing readability and integrating them closely into the narrative—by explicitly discussing what they show and how they support the argument—would greatly improve clarity. - It would be helpful to state the paper's original contribution more explicitly. The ABC classification seems to rely purely on item frequency. Clarifying the exact criterion and briefly justifying this choice would strengthen the methodology. - Similarly, providing a short justification for the XYZ thresholds would add valuable context. - A brief description of how seasonal, new, obsolete, and intermittent demand items are handled would make the approach more complete and replicable. - The statement about achieving “complete inventory accuracy in real time” is too strong. While a WMS improves traceability and accuracy, it rarely eliminates all errors. A more nuanced formulation would be preferable.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer B:
The paper addresses a relevant industrial problem and presents an interesting approach combining cross-departmental collaboration, ABC-XYZ classification, production planning, and Warehouse Management Systems (WMS). The main strengths of the paper are its practical relevance, clear identification of the logistics challenges, and potential applicability in an industrial environment. However, some aspects could be further strengthened: i) The paper could clarify more explicitly what is novel in the proposed approach compared with existing methods and frameworks involving ABC-XYZ classification, WMS, and supply chain management. ii) Further methodological details would improve the clarity of the study, particularly regarding how the ABC-XYZ classification, safety stocks, minimum and maximum inventory levels, and demand variability are determined. iii) The paper mainly presents KPIs and target values, while providing limited quantitative evidence of the effectiveness of the proposed approach. If available, before-and-after results from FEAL would significantly strengthen the analysis and provide more convincing evidence of its practical impact. iv) Statements regarding the elimination of redundant inventory, improved accuracy, and increased profitability could be further supported by empirical evidence. Alternatively, these outcomes could be presented more cautiously as potential or expected benefits. v) The literature review could be expanded to provide a clearer research gap and better position the proposed approach in relation to existing studies. vi) A brief discussion of the main limitations of the study and the extent to which the proposed approach could be applied to other industrial contexts would further strengthen the manuscript. Overall, the paper addresses a relevant topic and demonstrates clear practical potential. Further strengthening the scientific positioning, methodological description, and empirical validation would enhance the quality and contribution of the manuscript.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ratings.value:
The paper addresses a relevant industrial problem and presents a practically interesting integrated approach combining cross-departmental collaboration, ABC-XYZ classification, inventory management, production planning, and WMS implementation. The industrial context is clearly described, and the approach has clear practical relevance and potential impact.
The main limitation is the limited validation of the proposed approach. The manuscript is largely conceptual and practice-oriented, with limited quantitative evidence demonstrating its effectiveness. In particular, the KPIs are mainly presented as target values rather than measured results, making it difficult to assess the actual impact of the approach.
The paper would also benefit from stronger positioning within the existing scientific literature and a clearer articulation of its contribution. As the individual methods employed are well established, the authors should clarify the added value of their integrated framework and how it extends existing approaches.
Overall, the paper has clear industrial relevance and practical potential. However, a stronger articulation of the scientific contribution and additional evidence supporting the effectiveness of the proposed approach would significantly strengthen the manuscript.

revisions.judgment_comment:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer A:
The manuscript addresses a highly relevant and timely topic, offering a valuable critical perspective on electrical conductor sizing. The core idea is interesting: it demonstrates that reducing copper usage does not automatically guarantee greater sustainability when conductor lifetime and Joule losses are factored into the equation. To strengthen the work and maximize its impact, I encourage the authors to refine the following aspects: - Detail the specific Arrhenius parameters and sources used, while clarifying how conductor temperature directly relates to expected lifetime. - Include a simple life-cycle or break-even analysis. The assumption that a 15% reduction in copper equals a 15% drop in cost and environmental impact should be framed more cautiously, as manufacturing variables play a role. - Clarify the assumptions behind the reported 17.75% increase in Joule losses. Additionally, explicitly state the regulatory criteria used to validate the 42.5 mm² section. - Acknowledge that replacing a conductor does not equal the full footprint of a brand-new cable, since copper is highly recyclable and retains significant economic value. - Conduct a careful English language review, ensure references strictly match the conference template, and check the missing reference.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer B:
for the authors
1-Please briefly indicate the main assumptions of the case study, particularly the conductor material and insulation type, installation conditions and operating regime. 2 -Please provide the Arrhenius parameters used to calculate the estimated conductor lifetimes or identify their exact source. 3 - Please verify the reported increase in Joule losses, since both 17.65% and 17.75% appear in the manuscript. 4 - The conclusions about economic and environmental benefits should be expressed more cautiously, as they depend on the load profile, operating time, energy cost and installation lifetime. 5 - Please add the missing reference [15], revise the English terminology—particularly “driver” instead of “conductor”—and replace the “X” in the footer with the correct page numbers.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Editor:

[To be corrected]

The authors are requested to address all necessary corrections identified during the review process and resubmit the revised manuscript by 21 September 2026, 23:59 (Lisbon local time).
For manuscripts prepared using Microsoft Word, the authors must also submit a ZIP file containing all figures as separate files, numbered according to their appearance in the manuscript (e.g., fig01.png, fig02.svg, fig03.png). The figures should be provided in high quality, preferably in vector format (SVG) whenever applicable.

comments.html:
Response to the Reviewers

We would like to thank the reviewers for their valuable comments and constructive suggestions. In the revised manuscript, we have strengthened the discussion by providing a more critical analysis of the results and the main technical bottlenecks affecting energy recovery at WWTPD. We have also added a dedicated “Study Limitations” subsection, clarifying the assumptions, literature-based projections, and the need for further plant-scale validation. In addition, minor improvements were made to the language, equations, numerical consistency, figure captions, units, and reference formatting. The scenario calculations and related values were carefully reviewed and corrected to ensure consistency throughout the manuscript. We believe that these revisions have improved the clarity, technical rigor, and overall quality of the paper

The results are relevant and support the main conclusions. However, the discussion could be strengthened by providing a more critical analysis of the results and explicitly addressing the study limitations. Minor improvements in language, figure presentation and references would also enhance the overall quality of the manuscript. Overall, this is a valuable contribution that merits publication after revision.

This is an interesting contribution with implications for international decarbonization goals. The research proposes six complementary strategies to improve the energy efficiency of wastewater treatment plants (WWTP). The work draws on a real case study from Durres, Albania and offers important benefits for WWTPs, because the proposed technology upgrades can be easily applied while avoiding major infrastructure reconstruction.

contribution.title: Energy Performance Assessment and Cost-Effective Retrofit Measures for a Hotel Building: A Portuguese Case Study

revisions.judgment_comment:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer A:
The paper presents a clear and relevant assessment of the energy performance of a real hotel building, combining energy certification, measurement-informed dynamic simulation, and economic evaluation of retrofit measures. The analysis of the photovoltaic system, roof insulation, and boiler replacement is well structured, and the comparison of their energy, certification, and economic impacts provides useful practical insights for retrofit decision-making. Overall, the paper makes a valuable contribution by demonstrating how measurement-informed simulation and the Portuguese energy certification framework can be combined to support transparent and practically relevant prioritization of energy-efficiency measures in hotel buildings.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer B:
This research exemplifies the application of three retrofit measures in a hotel building in Portugal. The retrofit outcomes show improved building’s energy performance, with interesting payback periods. Although the scientific originality is moderate, these results are readily applicable to similar building typologies and contribute to decarbonization goals.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Editor:

[Accepted]
The paper has been accepted for publication.
For manuscripts prepared using Microsoft Word, the authors are requested to submit a ZIP file containing all figures as separate files, numbered according to their appearance in the manuscript (e.g., fig01.png, fig02.svg, fig03.png). The figures should be provided in high quality, preferably in vector format (SVG) whenever applicable.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

comments.html:
We thank both reviewers for their constructive feedback.
Reviewer A: We thank the reviewer for the positive assessment.
Reviewer B:
1) Dimensional consistency of Eqs. (2) and (4): Thank you for catching this. The parentheses around (e_Δt − f_Δt) were present in the Word source but were dropped during PDF export/rendering, making the term appear as a bare subtraction of an emission factor from an emission quantity. We have verified the equation objects directly and confirmed the parentheses are correctly in place; a corrected PDF will be generated to ensure both terms display properly. The underlying calculations were not affected — only the visual rendering of the submitted PDF was. We have also harmonized units to MWh throughout Section 2 (previously "kWh" appeared once in the definition of R_t,Δt).
2) Sensitivity analysis: We have added a statement clarifying that the four scenarios already constitute a 2×2 sensitivity design over the two most influential drivers (electricity demand and RES capacity growth), spanning 249.8–299.9 MtCO₂. We further note that Eqs. (2) and (4) are linear in both the emission factor e_Δt and the loss factor δ_p,Δt, so that a proportional variation in either propagates approximately linearly into the avoided-emissions estimate. A full parametric sweep of these secondary parameters is identified as future work (Section 3.5).
3) Justification of modelling assumptions: We have added a paragraph (Section 2.4) justifying the constant natural-gas emission factor assumption — following Portugal's 2022 coal phase-out, natural gas is the only remaining large-scale dispatchable fossil technology, and shows a strong negative correlation (−0.75) with renewable generation, consistent with its marginal position in the MIBEL merit order. We have also explicitly acknowledged, as a limitation, that the assumption of RES systematically reducing network losses holds under moderate penetration, and that reverse power flows under highly concentrated, high-penetration scenarios — not captured by the present model — could offset this benefit; this is left for future work.
4) Figure 3 readability: We agree that splitting Figure 3 into two figures would improve readability. However, given the strict 5-page conference limit, this would require removing other content we consider important for the completeness of the paper. We have therefore kept the figure as a single panel in this version, and would welcome the opportunity to present the split figure in an extended journal version of this work.

revisions.judgment_comment:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer A:
The manuscript presents a relevant and clearly motivated methodology for improving carbon accounting by incorporating avoided transmission and distribution losses. Its principal strengths are the practical application to the Portuguese power system, the consideration of different long-term scenarios, and the clear quantitative comparison with the conventional generation-displacement approach. The results provide useful evidence of the importance of network losses in renewable energy assessments. Overall, the manuscript is appropriate for acceptance for conference presentation.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer B:
The manuscript addresses a scientifically and technically relevant topic and provides an interesting contribution by incorporating network losses and RES connection voltage levels into avoided-emission estimates. The application to the Portuguese power system and the 15-minute temporal resolution add practical value. The results are generally well presented and internally consistent. Some recommendations: 1) Verify the dimensional consistency of Eqs. (2) and (4). An emission quantity, (R x e), is currently subtracted from (f_Delta t), defined as an emission factor, which is dimensionally inconsistent. The authors should correct the formulation and clarify whether this issue is only typographical or affects the calculations and results. Units should also be harmonized throughout the manuscript, particularly between kWh and MWh. 2) Include a sensitivity analysis to assess the robustness of the reported 11.5–16% improvement. At minimum, low/medium/high cases should be considered for the most influential uncertain parameters, including demand and capacity projections, loss parameters, voltage-level allocation, and emission factors. 3) Better justify and discuss the main modelling assumptions, particularly that renewable generation systematically reduces network losses and that displaced conventional generation can be represented using a constant natural-gas emission factor. These assumptions should also be explicitly acknowledged as limitations. 4) Improve Figure 3 readability. The current combination of numerous curves and two vertical axes is difficult to interpret. Consider separating absolute avoided emissions and the relative benefit of accounting for network losses into two figures with fewer curves. Overall, the work has good potential, but these issues should be addressed to strengthen its scientific robustness and reproducibility.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Editor:

[To be corrected]

The authors are requested to address all necessary corrections identified during the review process and resubmit the revised manuscript by 21 September 2026, 23:59 (Lisbon local time).
For manuscripts prepared using Microsoft Word, the authors must also submit a ZIP file containing all figures as separate files, numbered according to their appearance in the manuscript (e.g., fig01.png, fig02.svg, fig03.png). The figures should be provided in high quality, preferably in vector format (SVG) whenever applicable.

comments.html:
We thank the reviewers for their constructive comments. Numerical ranges have been standardised throughout the manuscript, and the Introduction now clarifies the study’s contribution in relation to previous work. We have clarified that filament diameter was monitored for all formulations, with only the 3 wt% CNC profile presented for brevity. The discussion now distinguishes experimental observations from possible mechanisms and explicitly states that reduced elongation at break does not establish increased stiffness, as Young’s modulus was not evaluated. Wettability measurements are clearly identified as referring to compression-moulded films, and the 24 h interval is described as a practical testing reference rather than evidence of complete stabilisation.

To improve the presentation of mechanical results, Table 3 has been replaced by a two-panel figure showing mean tensile strength and elongation at break with sample standard deviation error bars.

Regarding statistical analysis, given the five-page limit, we have retained a descriptive comparison and explicitly acknowledged that statistical significance was not assessed. The approximately 5% increase at 3 wt% CNC therefore refers to the observed mean tensile strength and is not presented as a statistically significant improvement.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer A:
The notation of numerical ranges should be corrected throughout the paper. All numerical ranges should be written in the following form: “from 0.05 mm to 0.30 mm” rather than: “0.05–0.30 mm”. Best regards
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer B:
This paper presents a relevant study on PLA/CNC composites for FFF 3D printing. The topic is interesting and the experimental work is clear, with results generally supporting the conclusions. A few points could improve the manuscript: • The original contribution should be stated more clearly in relation to previous PLA/CNC studies. • A statistical analysis would help confirm the significance of the differences observed, particularly for the 3 wt% CNC formulation. • The authors should clarify why filament diameter was analysed only for the 3 wt% CNC formulation. • The discussion should clearly distinguish experimental findings from proposed explanations, such as CNC dispersion, agglomeration, nucleation, and alignment. • The authors should clarify the interpretation of the mechanical results, particularly regarding elongation and stiffness. • It should be clearly stated that the wettability tests were performed on compression-moulded films, not directly on printed specimens. • The discussion of ageing could better acknowledge that the material may continue to change after 24 h. • The mechanical results could be presented more clearly, using graphs with error bars and statistical comparisons where appropriate. Overall, this is a clear and relevant conference paper. These points are mainly suggestions to improve the clarity and robustness of the manuscript and do not affect its suitability for the conference.

ratings.value:
This paper presents a relevant study on PLA/CNC composites for FFF 3D printing. The topic is interesting and the experimental work is clear, with results generally supporting the conclusions.
A few points could improve the manuscript:
•	The original contribution should be stated more clearly in relation to previous PLA/CNC studies.
•	A statistical analysis would help confirm the significance of the differences observed, particularly for the 3 wt% CNC formulation.
•	The authors should clarify why filament diameter was analysed only for the 3 wt% CNC formulation.
•	The discussion should clearly distinguish experimental findings from proposed explanations, such as CNC dispersion, agglomeration, nucleation, and alignment.
•	The authors should clarify the interpretation of the mechanical results, particularly regarding elongation and stiffness.
•	It should be clearly stated that the wettability tests were performed on compression-moulded films, not directly on printed specimens.
•	The discussion of ageing could better acknowledge that the material may continue to change after 24 h.
•	The mechanical results could be presented more clearly, using graphs with error bars and statistical comparisons where appropriate.
Overall, this is a clear and relevant conference paper. These points are mainly suggestions to improve the clarity and robustness of the manuscript and do not affect its suitability for the conference.

ratings.value:
The paper presents a relevant and timely study on PLA/CNC composites for FFF 3D printing. The topic is well suited to the conference, particularly in the areas of additive manufacturing, polymer composites, and sustainable materials.
The experimental work is clear and coherent, and the results are generally well supported by the methodology. The study shows that the addition of 3 wt% CNC leads to a modest improvement in tensile strength, while lower CNC contents do not provide a clear improvement.
The main limitation is that the novelty is moderate, as similar PLA/CNC systems have already been studied. The relatively small number of specimens and the lack of statistical significance testing also limit the strength of some conclusions. However, these limitations are acceptable for a conference paper.
Overall, the paper is well structured, technically sound, and relevant to the conference. Only minor revisions are needed, mainly to clarify the originality of the work and improve the presentation and discussion of the results.

comments.html:
[Response to Reviewers:]
We thank the reviewers for the positive assessment and for the constructive suggestions. In the revised manuscript, we have made the following changes: clarified that the validation consists of controller-level functional tests with simulated sensor inputs, rather than long-term field trials with physical operation of the thermal sources and storage tank; added a table summarising the functional scenarios, expected controller actions, and observed actions; reported the main controller and test parameters; revised the figures and their captions; moderated the statements concerning economic performance and emphasised that quantitative economic assessment is future work; clarified the biomass-boiler availability criterion and the treatment of the heat-pump COP; and arranged the keywords alphabetically and performed an editorial revision.

[Response to Editors:]
In the revised manuscript, we made edits to remove duplicated sentences, standardise notation and terminology, and improve figure captions and cross-references.

revisions.judgment_comment:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer A:

Good topic. Good paper.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer B:
The paper presents a relevant and practical contribution within the scope of the conference. The proposed low-cost controller and its integration of local measurements, weather information, electricity prices, and multiple heat sources are of interest. A few revisions would improve the clarity and overall quality of the manuscript. (i) Please strengthen the presentation of the functional validation using the tests already performed. A compact table summarising the main operating scenarios, expected controller action, and observed action would make the Results section clearer. (ii) Please report the main parameters used in the controller and tests, particularly Tmin, Tconf, Tmax, hysteresis, boiler efficiency, pellet LHV, electrical heater efficiency, and the heat-pump COP. (iii) Please revise Figure 3 so that it is clear that the image on the right corresponds to the controller graphical user interface. The two panels could be labelled “(a) Assembled controller prototype” and “(b) Controller graphical user interface”. (iv) Please improve the overall quality of the figures. Computer-generated figures should preferably be provided in vector format, or alternatively as high-resolution PNG files. Particular attention should be given to Figure 2. (v) Statements concerning economic performance should be slightly moderated, since the present work demonstrates functional operation, while the quantitative economic comparison is identified as future work. (vi) Please briefly clarify the biomass-boiler availability criterion based on Tflow > Treturn and revise the general statement that the heat-pump COP is “always greater than one”. (vii) Please arrange the keywords alphabetically: Domestic hot water; Energy management; Hybrid thermal systems; Renewable energy; Smart control. (viii) A careful editorial revision is recommended to correct duplicated sentences, standardise notation and terminology, and improve the consistency of figure captions and references.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Editor:

[To be corrected]

The authors are requested to address all necessary corrections identified during the review process and resubmit the revised manuscript by 21 September 2026, 23:59 (Lisbon local time).
For manuscripts prepared using Microsoft Word, the authors must also submit a ZIP file containing all figures as separate files, numbered according to their appearance in the manuscript (e.g., fig01.png, fig02.svg, fig03.png). The figures should be provided in high quality, preferably in vector format (SVG) whenever applicable.

revisions.judgment_comment:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer A:
The manuscript presents a relevant laboratory PV monitoring platform, but several aspects should be clarified or strengthened: 1) Introduction: The introduction is somewhat broader than the actual contribution. It should be more focused on PV monitoring requirements, laboratory/educational needs, and the specific contribution of the proposed platform, while broader topics such as storage and intelligent energy management should be presented mainly as future applications. 2) Fault detection: The abstract claims fault-detection capability, but no detection algorithm, threshold, diagnostic procedure, fault-injection experiment, or detection result is presented. Monitoring electrical variables may enable future fault-detection applications, but does not itself demonstrate this capability. The authors should either remove this claim or provide at least a basic experimental demonstration of fault detection. 3) Table 3 – DC current: The reported value of 9.85 A requires clarification. Since the modules are connected in series, the string current should remain approximately equal to the module current (7.88 A). The value 9.85 A appears to result from applying a 1.25 safety factor. If so, this factor and the corresponding design standard or sizing rule should be explicitly stated. 4) Electrical protection and safety: Although the abstract mentions protection coordination, grounding, and safety measures, these aspects are insufficiently documented. A single-line electrical diagram showing DC/AC protections, disconnects, fuses, SPDs, grounding, current transformers, and measurement points would substantially improve the technical description. 5) Figure 2: The photograph confirms the physical implementation but would be more informative if annotated to identify the inverter, microinverter, analyzers, Raspberry Pi, protections, AC/DC panels, and local display.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Editor:

[To be corrected]

The authors are requested to address all necessary corrections identified during the review process and resubmit the revised manuscript by 21 September 2026, 23:59 (Lisbon local time).
For manuscripts prepared using Microsoft Word, the authors must also submit a ZIP file containing all figures as separate files, numbered according to their appearance in the manuscript (e.g., fig01.png, fig02.svg, fig03.png). The figures should be provided in high quality, preferably in vector format (SVG) whenever applicable.

contribution.title: Influence of the operating point on the life cycle environmental impacts of a thermoelectric module for cooling applications

revisions.judgment_comment:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer A:
The manuscript addresses a highly relevant and timely topic, offering an innovative perspective on the Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) of thermoelectric cooling (TEC) modules. The approach of using continuous response surfaces to evaluate environmental performance across the entire operating domain, rather than relying solely on single nominal conditions, is excellent and highly pertinent. The work is well-structured, clearly written, and technically sound. I would like to highlight, as a key strength, the holistic view the authors used to balance the absolute environmental results with the redistribution of life cycle stage shares. To help the authors further enhance the impact and clarity of this valuable contribution, I suggest considering the inclusion of a brief sentence in the discussion section explicitly guiding future researchers on how these dynamic variables could be integrated next
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer B:
We suggest that the authors include the missing details (commercial module model, specification of the use-phase electricity mix, and DC power supply efficiency assumptions) prior to the final version.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Editor:

[To be corrected]

The authors are requested to address all necessary corrections identified during the review process and resubmit the revised manuscript by 21 September 2026, 23:59 (Lisbon local time).

revisions.judgment_comment:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer A:
Dear Authors, please correct as follows: 1. Clearly compare unidirectional and bidirectional strategies or align the title with what was actually tested 2. Do not use "mechanical properties" if they only have microhardness 3. Be sure to use the paper writing template published on the conference page for authors 4.Thoroughly improve the English language throughout the paper Best regards
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer B:
The manuscript addresses a relevant WAAM topic and presents experimental work on deposition-path strategies, microstructural evolution and hardness. However, substantial revision is required before acceptance. (i) The relationship between the stated objective and the reported results should be strengthened. Although unidirectional and bidirectional strategies are presented as the main comparison, the Results and Discussion section does not provide a clear quantitative comparison between them. (ii) The experimental methodology requires additional detail to ensure reproducibility. Relevant information includes wire diameter, substrate material and dimensions, shielding gas and flow rate, travel speed, wire-feed speed, interlayer temperature or cooling time, layer height, and number of specimens. (iii) The original template instructions remain at the beginning of Section 3 and must be removed. (iv) The microstructural analysis is mainly qualitative. Quantitative indicators should be included where possible, and all micrographs should contain clear scale bars. (v) The microhardness methodology should specify the applied load, dwell time, measurement spacing, number of indentations and applicable test standard. (vi) Statements concerning improved yield strength should be removed or supported by appropriate mechanical testing. (vii) Figure numbering should be checked, particularly the references to Figures 4.14 and 4.15. (viii) Figure quality and consistency should be improved. Schematics should preferably use vector formats, while micrographs should use consistent labelling and scale information. (ix) The statement that deposits were produced “without any defects” should be reconciled with the reported waviness, plate distortion and height variation. (x) The English should be thoroughly revised for grammar, scientific style, terminology and consistent UK English. Major revision is recommended.

contribution.title: Geographic Sensitivity of LFC-Based SHIP Systems Under Different Industrial Load Profiles

revisions.judgment_comment:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer A:
It would be good to increase size of numbers and names of variables in figures. They are too small.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer B:
The paper presents a relevant and well-structured contribution within the scope of the conference. The methodology is clearly defined and the results provide useful insight into the geographic sensitivity of LFC-based SHIP systems under different industrial load profiles. A few revisions would improve the technical precision and clarity of the manuscript. (i) The LCOH/SF indicator should be better justified. As this is not a conventional economic indicator, the authors should clarify its interpretation, specify whether SF is used as a fraction or percentage, and state the resulting units. (ii) The manuscript refers to “IEA-SHC Task 59”, while reference [15] corresponds to IEA SHC Task 54; this inconsistency should be corrected. (iii) The statement “no OPEX degradation (d = 0)” should be revised, since d appears to represent degradation of useful energy output rather than OPEX. (iv) Please distinguish clearly between relative percentage changes and percentage-point differences, particularly when comparing the reported 31–36% improvements with the Delta SF values. (v) The stronger decline beyond 42°N should be discussed with some caution, since the number and distribution of valid grid nodes vary with latitude. (vi) The fixed system configuration should include the main physical characteristics of the 50 LFC loops and the principal TES/steam-generator parameters. (vii) The spatial interpolation method used in Figure 1 should be identified. (viii) The conclusion regarding transferability across the Peninsula should be slightly moderated, since only one fixed system configuration was analysed. (ix) Keywords should be lowercase, alphabetically ordered, and without acronyms: greenius; levelised cost of heat; linear Fresnel collector; load profile; solar heat for industrial processes; thermal energy storage.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ratings.value: The paper presents a relevant and well-structured contribution within the scope of the conference. The methodology is clearly defined and the results provide useful insight into the geographic sensitivity of LFC-based SHIP systems under different industrial load profiles. A few revisions would improve the technical precision and clarity of the manuscript. (i) The LCOH/SF indicator should be better justified. As this is not a conventional economic indicator, the authors should clarify its interpretation, specify whether SF is used as a fraction or percentage, and state the resulting units. (ii) The manuscript refers to “IEA-SHC Task 59”, while reference [15] corresponds to IEA SHC Task 54; this inconsistency should be corrected. (iii) The statement “no OPEX degradation (d = 0)” should be revised, since d appears to represent degradation of useful energy output rather than OPEX. (iv) Please distinguish clearly between relative percentage changes and percentage-point differences, particularly when comparing the reported 31–36% improvements with the Delta SF values. (v) The stronger decline beyond 42°N should be discussed with some caution, since the number and distribution of valid grid nodes vary with latitude. (vi) The fixed system configuration should include the main physical characteristics of the 50 LFC loops and the principal TES/steam-generator parameters. (vii) The spatial interpolation method used in Figure 1 should be identified. (viii) The conclusion regarding transferability across the Peninsula should be slightly moderated, since only one fixed system configuration was analysed. revisions.judgment_comment:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer A:
he manuscript addresses a practically relevant topic by discussing engineering modifications introduced during the execution of HVAC and technical installations. However, substantial revisions are required: • Add an abstract and keywords clearly presenting the objective, methodology, principal results, and contribution. • Correct the title typographical error: “Select ed” should be “Selected.” • Introduce a clear methodological framework and separate the case descriptions from the results and discussion. • Provide quantitative information for each case, including the original and revised designs, calculation assumptions, equipment specifications, costs, and commissioning or validation results. • Verify the stated H14 filtration efficiency against EN 1822-1 and clarify whether integral or local MPPS efficiency is being reported. • For the acoustic case, specify whether the reported values are sound pressure or sound power levels, include frequency weighting and operating conditions, and provide measured post-installation results. • Expand the literature review with recent studies and applicable technical standards for HVAC commissioning, controlled environments, gas installations, and acoustic performance. • Correct the citation order and placement; Reference [2] currently appears before [1], and several citations are placed after the sentence-ending punctuation. • Remove the duplicated numbering in the reference list and standardise the reference format. • Review the English, author and affiliation information, excessive word spacing, section structure, and the blank fourth page. Recommend revision before acceptance for presentation at the conference. The manuscript may be considered suitable after these issues have been satisfactorily addressed.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer B:
The manuscript addresses a relevant practical topic by presenting three real case studies involving HVAC and technical-installation modifications during the construction phase. Its main strength is the demonstration of how integrated engineering analysis can improve system safety, functionality, maintainability, and acoustic performance. However, the paper lacks an abstract, a clearly defined methodology, quantitative results, and adequate validation of the proposed modifications. The technical justification, literature review, English, citation order, reference formatting, and document structure also require improvement. The authors should conduct a proper review considering the previous recommendations.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

contribution.title: Physics-Informed Correction of RANS-Based CFD Fields for Backward-Facing Step Flow Using Hybrid Neural Networks

revisions.judgment_comment:
Reviewer A:
The paper presents a technically relevant and well-structured proof-of-concept within the scope of the conference. The comparison between a supervised MLP and a continuity-regularised PINN is clearly framed, and the limitations of using a higher-resolution RANS solution as the numerical reference are appropriately acknowledged. A few revisions would improve reproducibility and interpretation. (i) Please report the units of all error and divergence metrics in Tables 2 and 3, including velocity, pressure, and divergence quantities. (ii) Table 2 should include the coarse-field baseline errors used to calculate the reported percentage reductions, allowing these values to be directly verified. (iii) Please define the reference quantities used in the normalised validation score of Eq. (6) and briefly explain how the continuity-loss weight was selected. (iv) The train/validation/test splitting procedure should be described more explicitly, including the corresponding proportions and the role of the streamwise-coordinate quantile bins. (v) Since Table 3 reports divergence over the full aligned domain, it would be useful to also report or discuss the divergence performance on the held-out test partition, ensuring that the physical diagnostic is evaluated independently of training data. (vi) Please provide the principal CFD settings required for reproducibility, particularly inlet turbulence quantities, wall treatment, discretisation schemes, and convergence criteria. (vii) Since computational times are reported, the hardware used for the CFD simulations and neural-network training should be identified. (viii) Keywords should be lowercase, alphabetically ordered, and without acronyms: backward-facing step; computational fluid dynamics; continuity regularisation; physics-informed neural networks; Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes. (ix) Please reformulate the title for a more clear scope of the work.

Editor:

[To be corrected]

The authors are requested to address all necessary corrections identified during the review process and resubmit the revised manuscript by 21 September 2026, 23:59 (Lisbon local time).

contribution.title: Predictive monitoring; Rotating Machinery; Anomaly detection; K-CUSUM; RKHS

revisions.judgment_comment:
Reviewer A:
The paper addresses a relevant problem and presents an interesting adaptive condition-monitoring framework. However, several methodological, numerical, and bibliographic inconsistencies should be corrected before acceptance. (i) The reported detection performance is not fully consistent: the Abstract and Section 3.1 report detection five acquisitions after onset, whereas Table 1 reports seven acquisitions for the gated detector. Please clarify which result and configuration are representative. (ii) The event counts should also be reconciled, since Section 3.1 reports ten events while Table 1 reports nine alarms shown. The terms event, alarm, anomaly, and regime change should be defined and used consistently. (iii) Acquisition 532 should not be described as "ground truth", since the onset is inferred from vibration-derived indicators used in the analysis. It should instead be identified as a data-driven onset criterion. (iv) Please verify Eq. (2), which appears to correspond to an estimator of squared MMD rather than MMD itself. (v) The use of the Sidak correction requires clearer justification, since the individual tests are not necessarily independent. (vi) Please state whether standardisation, PCA, kernel bandwidth, and detection threshold are recalculated after baseline replacement, and provide the main implementation details of the ADF and trend tests. (vii) The claimed ability to distinguish legitimate operating-regime changes from degradation is not directly validated on the selected constant-operating-condition dataset and should be presented more cautiously. (viii) The references require careful revision. Reference [5] contains "Authors to be confirmed" and must be verified (???????). Reference [8] should be replaced by its peer-reviewed version where available. Preprints are not acceptable in the final manuscript. All references should be checked for correct authorship, title, publication details, DOI, and consistent formatting. (ix) Any use of LLMs must be disclosed, and the authors remain responsible for the final text. The english language is very poor and must be revised.

Reviewer B:
The manuscript addresses a relevant power system planning problem by incorporating avoided transmission and distribution losses into the assessment of emission reductions from renewable generation. Its principal strengths are the methodological contribution, the 15-minute temporal resolution, and its application to four long-term scenarios for the Portuguese power system. The main limitations concern the simplified representation of the network. Nevertheless, the study provides technically relevant and useful results for decarbonisation planning, supporting its acceptance for presentation at the conference.

Editor:

[To be corrected]

The authors are requested to address all necessary corrections identified during the review process and resubmit the revised manuscript by 21 September 2026, 23:59 (Lisbon local time).

contribution.title: A conservative Euler–Lagrange conversion framework for primary atomisation: morphological classification and linear-stability fragmentation on adaptive parallel meshes

revisions.judgment_comment:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer A:
The paper presents a technically strong and well-structured contribution within the scope of the conference. The proposed Euler-Lagrange conversion framework is clearly described, and the integration of morphological classification, linear-stability fragmentation, AMR, and MPI decomposition is of particular interest. A few revisions would improve the technical precision and reproducibility of the manuscript. (i) Since conservation is a central claim of the work, please report a quantitative momentum-conservation error or tolerance in addition to the mass ratio already presented. This would provide direct numerical evidence that both conserved quantities are preserved by the implementation. (ii) The interpretation of the morphological threshold should be slightly clarified. The choice of an aspect-ratio threshold of approximately 3 is physically motivated by the Rayleigh-Plateau instability criterion, but it would be preferable to present it as an approximation derived from this physical argument rather than as the exact stability limit. (iii) Please clarify the units and dimensional basis of all parameters introduced in the verification campaign, particularly those used in Eq. (6), so that the test cases can be reproduced unambiguously. (iv) The refinement study should emphasise that convergence is demonstrated only for sufficiently forced cases, while the low-Weber-number sinusoid remains mesh-sensitive, as already acknowledged in the manuscript. (v) Please ensure consistent decimal notation throughout the paper, using decimal points in accordance with English-language scientific conventions. (vi) Keywords should be lowercase, alphabetically ordered, and without acronyms: euler-lagrange coupling; linear stability analysis; primary atomisation; volume-of-fluid.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Editor:

[To be corrected]

The authors are requested to address all necessary corrections identified during the review process and resubmit the revised manuscript by 21 September 2026, 23:59 (Lisbon local time).

ratings.value: The paper presents a technically strong and well-structured contribution within the scope of the conference. The proposed Euler-Lagrange conversion framework is clearly described, and the integration of morphological classification, linear-stability fragmentation, AMR, and MPI decomposition is of particular interest. A few revisions would improve the technical precision and reproducibility of the manuscript. (i) Since conservation is a central claim of the work, please report a quantitative momentum-conservation error or tolerance in addition to the mass ratio already presented. This would provide direct numerical evidence that both conserved quantities are preserved by the implementation. (ii) The interpretation of the morphological threshold should be slightly clarified. The choice of an aspect-ratio threshold of approximately 3 is physically motivated by the Rayleigh-Plateau instability criterion, but it would be preferable to present it as an approximation derived from this physical argument rather than as the exact stability limit. revisions.judgment_comment:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer A:
The paper presents a relevant and practical case study on electric vehicle charging infrastructure for a higher education institution. The proposed hybrid AC/DC configuration and the assessment of transformer reinforcement and BESS-supported expansion are appropriate for the conference. A few revisions would improve technical clarity, reproducibility, and presentation. (i) The 125 kVA allocation is based on measurements collected between 9 and 23 March 2026. Please acknowledge that this short monitoring period may not capture seasonal or academic-year variations and clarify that 125 kVA is a conservative design criterion rather than a definitive capacity limit. (ii) Please provide the main assumptions used for cable and protection dimensioning, particularly cable lengths, installation method, correction factors, and the basis for the adopted current-carrying capacities. (iii) Section 2.3 states that IB, IN, I'Z, and I2 were determined, but Table 3 reports only part of these quantities; please include the missing values or revise the text accordingly. (iv) The BESS assessment should be identified as a preliminary power and energy-capacity analysis, since no time-series simulation of state of charge, charging demand, or energy-management strategy is presented. (v) Please clarify the practical basis for selecting the 100 kW DC + 22 kW AC configuration beyond installed power alone. (vi) Correct the table numbering in Section 3, where the sensitivity-analysis table is identified as “Table 2”. (vii) Please improve the quality and consistency of the figures. Schematics should preferably be redrawn using AutoCAD, TikZ/LaTeX, or another vector-graphics tool, using Computer Modern or a visually consistent font where possible. Figures should be supplied as SVG or another vector format, or as high-resolution PNG/TIFF when raster graphics are required. (viii) Keywords should be lowercase, alphabetically ordered, and without acronyms: battery energy storage system; electric vehicle charging infrastructure; higher education institution; smart energy management; sustainable mobility.

comments.html:
We sincerely thank the Reviewer for the constructive comments and suggestions, which helped improve the technical clarity, reproducibility, and presentation of the manuscript. The manuscript has been revised accordingly.

In particular, the revised version now explicitly acknowledges the limitations of the two-week monitoring period and clarifies that the 125 kVA allocation represents a conservative design criterion rather than a definitive capacity limit of PT1. The electrical validation section has been expanded to provide the main assumptions used for cable and protection dimensioning, including reference installation method D, underground installation in ducts, soil temperature, soil thermal-resistivity conditions, correction factors, and circuit lengths, in accordance with the RTIEBT. Table 3 has also been extended to include the relevant electrical quantities used for conductor and protection coordination.

The BESS assessment is now explicitly identified as a preliminary power- and energy-capacity analysis, clarifying that no time-series simulation of charging demand, state of charge, or energy-management strategy was performed. Dear Editor and Reviewer A,

Thank you for the constructive comments. All seven points have been addressed in the revised manuscript, as summarised below.

(i) The term "HCL" has been moderated throughout. The abstract, introduction and conclusions now describe the work as an HCL-oriented lighting design, and the conclusions state explicitly that the study demonstrates visual and energy performance, while the non-visual effects motivating the approach were not verified.

(ii) A convention distinguishing simulated, estimated and measured quantities has been added to Section 2.4 together with a note that the existing installation is characterised entirely by estimated values. Table entries are now marked accordingly.

(iii) Section 2.4 now states that the 2330-hour basis corresponds to continuous annual operation, that the academic calendar of 30 to 35 weeks amounts to roughly 1520 hours, and quantifies the effect: annual consumption would fall to approximately 1990 kWh for the existing installation and 1150 kWh for the proposed system without control, with the controlled figure somewhat above the proportional value since the excluded summer months are those of greatest daylight availability. (v) The narrow uniformity margin is discussed in Section 3.1 and is now also noted in the conclusions as a practical sensitivity of the layout.

(vi) Figure 1 has been replaced with a high-resolution version that i took from DIALux and is supplied as a separate file in the ZIP archive.

(vii) Keywords have been replaced with the list provided.

Yours sincerely,
André Rodrigues

revisions.judgment_comment:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer A:
The paper presents a relevant and practical study on the redesign of classroom lighting using tunable-white LED luminaires, daylight compensation, presence detection, and DALI-2 control. The work is suitable for the scope of the conference, but a few revisions would improve its technical precision and presentation. (i) The manuscript should moderate the use of the term “Human Centric Lighting” when discussing demonstrated performance. Since melanopic quantities were not calculated and no occupant evaluation was performed, the study demonstrates the visual and energy performance of an HCL-oriented design rather than verified non-visual or circadian benefits. (ii) Please distinguish more clearly between measured, simulated, and estimated quantities, particularly for the existing installation, whose illuminance and system power are not directly measured. (iii) The energy analysis uses approximately 2330 annual operating hours, while the classroom is stated to operate over a 30–35 week academic year. Please clarify this difference and, if possible, indicate its effect on annual consumption and savings. (iv) The use of Porto climate data for Viseu should remain explicitly identified as a limitation in the interpretation of daylight-related results. (v) The small uniformity margin of 0.61 versus the 0.60 requirement should be highlighted as a practical sensitivity of the proposed layout. (vi) Please improve the overall graphical quality of the manuscript. Figures should be provided in high quality, preferably as SVG or another suitable vector format, or as high-resolution PNG or TIFF files when raster images are required. All labels and graphical elements should remain clearly readable at the final publication size. (vii) Keywords should be lowercase and alphabetically ordered: energy efficiency; human centric lighting; intelligent lighting control; lighting engineering; sustainability.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

contribution.title: A Parametric Computational Framework for Aircraft Wetted Area Calculation and Zero-Lift Drag Estimation from 2D Layouts

files.filename: A Parametric Computational Framework for Aircraft.zip
A Parametric Computational Framework for Aircraft.pdf

revisions.judgment_comment:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer A:
The manuscript presents a useful computational framework for estimating aircraft wetted area and zero-lift drag from 2D layouts. However, several issues should be addressed before acceptance. (i) The main weakness is the lack of proper validation. The Diamond DA62 is presented as a validation case, but no comparison is provided against published wetted-area data, experimental drag data, CFD results, OpenVSP, or another established method. Therefore, the accuracy of the framework cannot yet be demonstrated. (ii) The aerodynamic calculation methodology is insufficiently reproducible. The authors should report the flight condition, Reynolds and Mach numbers, surface roughness values, assumed laminar-flow percentages, interference factors, reference area, and miscellaneous drag contributions used to obtain CD0. (iii) The mesh-generation and Boolean-union procedures require further detail, including the software libraries used, mesh resolution, convergence assessment, and treatment of failed or ambiguous intersections. (iv) The assumption that material selection directly determines laminar-flow extent should be better justified, since transition also depends on surface quality, contamination, Reynolds number and pressure gradients. (v) The use of generic symmetric NACA profiles when actual airfoil data are unavailable introduces uncertainty that should be quantified or discussed. (vi) The reported baseline fuselage wetted area is inconsistent, with values of 27.27 m² and 27.21 m² appearing in different sections. (vii) The conclusion that zero-lift drag is generally more sensitive to fuselage diameter than length should be moderated, as it is derived from a single aircraft and limited parametric cases. (viii) Figure quality should be improved substantially. Several plots have very small text and limited readability. Vector graphics should be used where possible. (ix) The English should be revised for consistent UK English and scientific style. Major revision is recommended.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Editor:

[To be corrected]

The authors are requested to address all necessary corrections identified during the review process and resubmit the revised manuscript by 21 September 2026, 23:59 (Lisbon local time).

contribution.title: ACM Framework™: An Integrated Methodology for Asset Criticality Assessment and Strategic Maintenance Decision-Making

revisions.judgment_comment:
Reviewer A:
The manuscript addresses a relevant issue in maintenance management and presents a clear conceptual structure for integrating asset criticality assessment with strategic maintenance decision-making. The proposed ACM Framework is easy to understand and has potential practical value. However, several methodological aspects should be strengthened before publication. The main concern is that the framework currently provides a well-defined process for scoring and classifying asset criticality, but the link between the resulting Criticality Level and the actual selection of maintenance strategies remains largely conceptual. The mathematical formulation also requires clarification. With criteria scored from 1 to 5 and normalised weights summing to 1, multiplying the weighted score by 20 produces a range of 20–100, rather than 0–100 as stated. Finally, the manuscript would benefit substantially from an application example or industrial case study, together with sensitivity analysis and, if possible, comparison with an established criticality assessment method. At present, the framework is promising, but its effectiveness and robustness have not yet been empirically demonstrated.

Reviewer B:
The paper proposes a relevant framework for linking multicriteria asset criticality assessment with strategic maintenance decision support. The topic is appropriate for the conference, but several points should be clarified to strengthen the methodological consistency and practical applicability of the work. (i) Please revise the ACM Score equation. The manuscript states that the weighting factors sum to 100%, while the equation multiplies the weighted sum by 20. If weights are expressed as percentages, this does not produce a 0–100 score. The mathematical formulation and weight convention should therefore be corrected and illustrated with a simple numerical example. (ii) Please clarify the resulting score range. With criteria scored from 1 to 5, the minimum normalised score appears to be 20 rather than 0, which should be reconciled with the proposed criticality intervals. (iii) The claimed integration between criticality assessment and maintenance strategy selection should be made more explicit. A compact decision matrix linking each Criticality Level to recommended maintenance strategies, inspection frequency, prioritisation, or resource allocation would considerably strengthen the framework. (iv) Since no industrial validation is presented, the manuscript should clearly frame the work as a proposed conceptual methodology and avoid implying demonstrated effectiveness. A small illustrative example using hypothetical assets would improve practical understanding without requiring a full case study. (v) The literature review should better justify the proposed weighting ranges and criticality thresholds. (vi) Please improve figure quality, preferably using vector formats such as SVG, or high-resolution PNG/TIFF where appropriate. (vii) Keywords should be lowercase, alphabetically ordered, and without acronyms: asset criticality; asset management; maintenance management; maintenance strategy; multicriteria decision-making.

The manuscript addresses a relevant issue in maintenance management and presents a clear conceptual structure for integrating asset criticality assessment with strategic maintenance decision-making. The proposed ACM Framework is easy to understand and has potential practical value. However, several methodological aspects should be strengthened before publication.
The main concern is that the framework currently provides a well-defined process for scoring and classifying asset criticality, but the link between the resulting Criticality Level and the actual selection of maintenance strategies remains largely conceptual.
The mathematical formulation also requires clarification. With criteria scored from 1 to 5 and normalised weights summing to 1, multiplying the weighted score by 20 produces a range of 20–100, rather than 0–100 as stated.
Finally, the manuscript would benefit substantially from an application example or industrial case study, together with sensitivity analysis and, if possible, comparison with an established criticality assessment method. At present, the framework is promising, but its effectiveness and robustness have not yet been empirically demonstrated.

Reviewer A:
The manuscript presents a relevant real world case study supported by hourly modelling and Monte Carlo analysis. Before publication, the authors should correct the inconsistencies in the reported waste volume and Spearman correlation, strengthen the justification of the assumptions, and improve the quality and legibility of the figures. In tehe text, references must be placed before punctuation and numbered in ascending order, correcting the sequence from [13] to [12] and the subsequent jump from [13] to [16]. The manuscript should also be shortened to comply with the conference page limit. Subject to these revisions, I recommend acceptance for presentation.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer B:
This research presents an interesting comparison of alternatives for district heating using energy recovered from a waste-to-energy plant. The objectives are strongly aligned with the European Union’s circular economy and decarbonization goals. The methodology is scientifically robust, using an uncertainty and risk assessment based on several key input parameters. The results show that the economic viability of different waste valorization routes depends on the parameters assessed, and highlight the importance of winter revenues, often underestimated in annual-average approaches.

contribution.title: Design and Computational Structural Evaluation of a Baja SAE Tubular Spaceframe

revisions.judgment_comment:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer A:
The manuscript presents a relevant structural assessment of a Baja SAE tubular spaceframe and adopts an efficient hybrid beam–shell modelling strategy. However, several issues should be addressed before acceptance. (i) The use of linear static analysis should be more carefully justified. In the frontal and side-impact cases, the reported stresses exceed the material yield strength, and in the side impact they also exceed the ultimate tensile strength. A linear elastic model cannot reliably predict post-yield behaviour or rupture. (ii) Consequently, the statement that rupture is predicted at the SIM–LFS weld should be moderated or supported by a non-linear material model. (iii) The conclusion that occupant protection is preserved should also be stated more cautiously, particularly for side impact, because the reported displacements are obtained from a linear model despite predicted yielding. (iv) The use of crash-pulse durations from a Volkswagen T-Cross to derive equivalent loads for a Baja SAE vehicle requires stronger justification and should be discussed as a limitation. (v) The hybrid beam–shell coupling procedure should be described in greater detail, including element types, connection formulation, shell thickness, weld representation and treatment of heat-affected zones. (vi) The mesh convergence procedure should state the convergence criterion and explain how local stress singularities were excluded. (vii) Verification using only a simply supported bumper tube does not fully verify the global frame model or beam–shell interfaces. This limitation should be acknowledged. (viii) The figures have insufficient quality for scientific publication. ANSYS results should be regenerated at higher resolution, with readable legends, scales, labels and annotations. Vector graphics should be used where possible. (ix) The literature review should better position the methodology relative to previous Baja SAE chassis studies. (x) The English should be revised for consistent UK English and scientific style.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Editor:

[To be corrected]

The authors are requested to address all necessary corrections identified during the review process and resubmit the revised manuscript by 21 September 2026, 23:59 (Lisbon local time).

comments.html:
Dear Editor and Reviewer,

We thank you for the careful review. The revised manuscript addresses all ten comments, as summarised below.

Important correction: while preparing the revision, we found that the submitted manuscript described the discretisation incorrectly. The model uses BEAM189 beam elements throughout, with SURF156 elements used only to apply the loads; no shell elements were used. The beam-shell approach had been discussed among the authors as a possible refinement, but was never implemented. The Abstract, Section 2.2, Section 3.3 and the Conclusions have been rewritten accordingly.

(i) Linear static analysis: justification and limits added (Section 2.3). Stresses above the yield strength are now presented as indicators of yielding, not as quantitative predictions.
(ii) Rupture at the SIM-LFS weld: the claim has been withdrawn. The junction is identified as the critical region, without predicting rupture (Section 3.3).
(iii) Occupant protection: the conclusion has been withdrawn for the side impact. Displacements are compared with the RATBSB clearances in Table 2, and the side-impact value is stated as a lower bound (Section 3.5).
(iv) T-Cross crash pulse: justification and limitation added (Section 2.3).
(v) Beam-shell coupling: see the correction above. The representation of the joints and its consequences are now described (Section 2.2).
(vi) Mesh convergence: the 0.5 % criterion is stated, and stress singularities are discussed (Section 2.2).
(vii) Verification: its single-member scope is acknowledged (Section 3.1).
(viii) Figures: rebuilt with vector legends in English, legible at print size. The displacement plots were replaced by Table 2, and the roll-over stress plot and the CAD rendering were omitted to respect the 5-page limit.
(ix) Literature: the methodology is now positioned against previous Baja SAE studies (Introduction), with one new reference.
(x) Language: revised for UK English and scientific style; several passages were condensed.

Kind regards,
Gabriel Bianchini Matos, on behalf of all authors

contribution.title: Sizing and Modeling of a 4x4 System Applied to a Baja SAE Vehicle

revisions.judgment_comment:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer A:
The manuscript presents a relevant and practically oriented design of a 4×4 traction system for a Baja SAE vehicle. However, several issues should be addressed before acceptance. (i) The shaft stress equations should be checked. As written, the bending and torsion expressions appear dimensionally inconsistent because the second moment of area and polar moment terms use d³ rather than d⁴. (ii) The drivetrain design should be linked more clearly to vehicle-level requirements. The overall transmission ratio, wheel torque, tractive force and design condition used to demonstrate off-road capability should be provided. (iii) Some shaft fatigue safety factors are only slightly above 1.2. The justification for this minimum value should be strengthened, particularly considering shock loading and manufacturing uncertainties. (iv) The bearing-life results require clarification. Some predicted lives are only 183–204 h, while the abstract refers to approximately two years of service. The assumed operating hours and relation to the stated three-competition durability should be demonstrated. (v) The FEA methodology should provide mesh size, convergence assessment, contact definitions, boundary conditions and load derivation. (vi) For gear verification, comparing contact stress directly with yield strength is not an adequate contact-fatigue criterion. The numerical results should instead be related to the allowable contact and bending stresses used in the analytical sizing. (vii) The mechanical properties adopted for additively manufactured 5183 aluminium should be justified for the actual manufacturing process and material condition. (viii) The figures require substantial improvement. Several SolidWorks and Excel screenshots are low-resolution and difficult to read. Results should be regenerated with clear scales, labels and preferably vector graphics where applicable. (ix) The literature review is very limited and should better position the proposed design relative to previous Baja SAE drivetrain solutions. (x) The English should be revised for consistent UK English and scientific style.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Editor:

[To be corrected]

The authors are requested to address all necessary corrections identified during the review process and resubmit the revised manuscript by 21 September 2026, 23:59 (Lisbon local time).
For manuscripts prepared using Microsoft Word, the authors must also submit a ZIP file containing all figures as separate files, numbered according to their appearance in the manuscript (e.g., fig01.png, fig02.svg, fig03.png). The figures should be provided in high quality, preferably in vector format (SVG) whenever applicable.
