revisions.judgment_comment:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer A:
The paper presents a relevant and practical application of OEE using real industrial data, supported by valuable shop-floor information and an Excel-based tool. The manuscript is well structured, and the conclusions are generally consistent with the results. The following points could further strengthen the study: i) Clarify how the ideal/reference cycle times were determined, particularly for CNC Router 1, where an OEE of 115% is reported. ii) Justify the fixed two-minute allowance per unit used for the laser cutting machine, specifying the activities included and whether it applies per piece or per batch/order. iii) Provide additional information on the dataset, including the number of days, shifts, production orders, and observations, as well as the criteria for classifying downtime, setups, and other losses. iv) Where possible, report measures of variability and show the evolution of OEE and its components over time, particularly for the laser cutting machine. v) Relate the identified losses more explicitly to the Six Big Losses framework and, if possible, include a sensitivity analysis of setup-time reductions or SMED implementation on OEE. vi) Expand the discussion of the difference between theoretical and measured OEE for the press brake, highlighting the losses that can only be identified through shop-floor observations. Addressing these points would improve the manuscript’s methodological clarity, reproducibility, and practical contribution.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer B:
The paper presents a useful practical application of Overall Equipment Effectiveness using real industrial data and an accessible Excel-based monitoring tool. The contribution is suitable for the scope of the conference. A few minor revisions would improve clarity and presentation. (i) Please review the consistency of the OEE methodology and reporting. In particular, the notation used for Availability, Performance, Quality, and OEE should be consistent; Table 1 would benefit from including the Quality component; and the OEE value above 100% for CNC router 1 should be clearly explained as an indication that the adopted reference cycle time may require revision. The fixed two-minute setup allowance should also be briefly justified, since it directly affects the Performance component. (ii) Please indicate more clearly the observation period or number of production cycles considered for the different cases and support, or slightly moderate, the statement that 85% represents an excellent OEE benchmark. (iii) The manuscript would benefit from at least one figure that helps the reader understand the analysed system and workflow. For example, a simple schematic or flowchart could show the monitored machines or projects, the collection of production data, the Excel-based calculation of Availability, Performance, Quality, and OEE, and the identification of improvement opportunities. This figure could be prepared using TikZ/LaTeX, Inkscape, Ipe, or another vector-graphics tool. Figures should be supplied in high quality, preferably as SVG or another vector format, or as high-resolution PNG/TIFF files. Keywords should also be lowercase, alphabetically ordered, and corrected: continuous improvement; industrial engineering and management; industrial performance; overall equipment effectiveness; production systems.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Editor:

[To be corrected]

The authors are requested to address all necessary corrections identified during the review process and resubmit the revised manuscript by 21 September 2026, 23:59 (Lisbon local time).

The paper presents a relevant and practical application of OEE using real industrial data, supported by valuable shop-floor information and an Excel-based tool. The manuscript is well structured, and the conclusions are generally consistent with the results.
The following points could further strengthen the study:
i) Clarify how the ideal/reference cycle times were determined, particularly for CNC Router 1, where an OEE of 115% is reported.
ii) Justify the fixed two-minute allowance per unit used for the laser cutting machine, specifying the activities included and whether it applies per piece or per batch/order.
iii) Provide additional information on the dataset, including the number of days, shifts, production orders, and observations, as well as the criteria for classifying downtime, setups, and other losses.
iv) Where possible, report measures of variability and show the evolution of OEE and its components over time, particularly for the laser cutting machine.
v) Relate the identified losses more explicitly to the Six Big Losses framework and, if possible, include a sensitivity analysis of setup-time reductions or SMED implementation on OEE.
vi) Expand the discussion of the difference between theoretical and measured OEE for the press brake, highlighting the losses that can only be identified through shop-floor observations.
Addressing these points would improve the manuscript’s methodological clarity, reproducibility, and practical contribution.

ratings.value:
The paper presents a relevant industrial case study on the application of Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) using real shop-floor data. Its main strengths are the practical relevance of the topic, the use of real manufacturing data, and the development of a simple Excel-based tool to support performance monitoring and continuous improvement. The paper is clearly structured and provides useful insights into the predominance of performance- and setup-related losses.
Nevertheless, the scientific contribution is relatively limited, as the work mainly applies an established OEE methodology to an industrial case. Some methodological and technical issues also require attention, particularly the reported OEE value above 100%, the justification and treatment of the fixed two-minute setup allowance per piece, and the limited description of the data collection and validation procedures. The statistical treatment of the results is also limited.
Overall, the paper has clear practical value and is relevant to the scope of ETEME Conference. The identified weaknesses are mainly related to methodological rigour and validation rather than to the relevance or coherence of the study.

revisions.judgment_comment:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer A:
The manuscript addresses a relevant machining problem, but the experimental design and quantitative analysis are not sufficiently rigorous. (i) The comparison between ramp angles is confounded by substantially different cutting distances and machining times. After 20 ramps, the tools travelled approximately 9.54, 4.94 and 3.42 m for 1°, 2° and 3°, respectively. Tool wear should therefore be normalised against cutting distance, machining time or removed material, or the experimental design revised to permit an equivalent comparison. (ii) The cutting times in Table 1 are inconsistent with the stated feed rate of 5400 mm/min. The authors should recalculate these values and define whether additional tool movements are included. (iii) Tool wear is evaluated mainly from images. Quantitative wear measurements, measurement locations, uncertainty, repeatability and an applicable wear criterion or standard are required. (iv) The study does not establish tool life, despite using this term in the keywords. Either tool life must be experimentally determined or this terminology removed. (v) The vibration analysis requires the accelerometer model, sensitivity, mounting procedure, acquisition duration, filtering, anti-aliasing treatment and RMS calculation window. The reported RMS unit of m/s should also be corrected if acceleration is measured. (vi) “Time-domain vibration spectrum” should be replaced by appropriate terminology. Frequency-domain analysis would also be valuable, particularly around spindle and tooth-passing frequencies. (vii) Roughness results are presented without numerical datasets, dispersion measures or statistical analysis. The roughness parameter, cut-off, evaluation length, measurement direction, number of replicates and uncertainty must be reported. (viii) The claimed “clear correlation” between wear, vibration and roughness is unsupported without statistical correlation analysis. (ix) The duplicated EDS paragraph and caption errors must be corrected. (x) The literature review should be strengthened and the English revised throughout for consistent UK English and scientific style. Major revision is required.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The figures should be provided in high quality, preferably in vector format (SVG) whenever applicable.

revisions.judgment_comment:
Reviewer A:
The paper addresses a relevant topic and presents a potentially useful computational framework for battery thermal management. However, several revisions are needed to improve consistency, reproducibility, and presentation. (i) The scope stated in the Abstract should be aligned with the results actually presented. The Abstract refers to three PCM thicknesses, seven coolant flow rates, and three vibration frequencies, whereas the Results section does not provide the corresponding parametric comparison. The manuscript should either include these results or revise the Abstract, Methods, and Conclusions accordingly. (ii) The numerical model requires additional information for reproducibility, particularly the battery heat-generation model or imposed heat source, nanofluid concentration, PCM properties and thickness values, inlet flow conditions, and how mechanical vibration is implemented in ANSYS Fluent. Section 2.3 should also be renamed, since it mainly describes boundary conditions and thermophysical properties rather than governing equations. (iii) Please review Table 1, where “Element Size” appears to contain element counts rather than element dimensions, and clarify the mesh-selection criterion. The validation procedure should also state which quantity is compared with Wang et al. and how the reported ±5% error was calculated. (iv) Section 2.4 should be presented as continuous technical text rather than as a bullet-point list, maintaining consistent formatting with the rest of the manuscript. (v) Please improve figure quality and readability, preferably using SVG or another vector format, or high-resolution PNG/TIFF files. Reference [11] duplicates reference [10] and should be corrected. The country should also be added to the affiliation. (vi) Keywords should be reduced to five, presented in lowercase, alphabetically ordered, and without acronyms: battery thermal management system; computational investigation; integrated cooling system; lithium-ion battery pack; phase change material.

Reviewer B:
The manuscript addresses a relevant topic and proposes an interesting combination of liquid cooling, PCM, nanofluid, and mechanical vibration for battery thermal management. However, in its current form, the paper would benefit from substantial revision before publication. My main concern is the mismatch between the scope announced in the abstract and the results actually presented. The abstract refers to different PCM thicknesses, several coolant flow rates, and different vibration frequencies, but the Results section does not clearly show the influence of these parameters. The numerical methodology should also be described in greater detail to improve reproducibility. The Results and Discussion section is presently rather descriptive. A more quantitative comparison among the investigated configurations would strengthen the paper. The conclusions should also be made more cautious and directly supported by the results presented. Finally, the manuscript would benefit from an editorial revision, including clearer section organisation, improved figure presentation, correction of language issues, and checking of references.

comments.html:
Review (Pedro A. Marques)

  1. Scientific and Technical Relevance
    ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
  2. Originality and Contribution
    ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)
  3. Scientific and Technical Validity
    ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)
  4. Methodological Rigour and Reproducibility
    ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)
  5. Results and Validation
    ⭐⭐⭐☆ (3.5/5)
  6. Discussion, Conclusions and Limitations
    ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)
  7. Clarity and Quality of Scientific Presentation
    ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
  8. Research Integrity and Publication Ethics
    Yes

  9. Comments for the Authors
    This paper addresses a highly relevant and timely topic related to the decarbonization of hard-to-abate industrial sectors and the challenges posed by emerging carbon regulations such as the European Union Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM). The topic is of significant importance for both academia and industry and aligns very well with current international efforts towards sustainable industrial development and energy transition.
    The manuscript provides a comprehensive review of the decarbonization challenges faced by key industrial sectors, including steel, cement, chemicals, fertilizers, aviation, and freight transport. The proposed renewable energy-powered supply chain framework successfully combines several important technologies, including renewable energy generation, green hydrogen production, energy storage systems, microgrids, and digital carbon monitoring. This integrated perspective represents one of the main strengths of the paper.
    The paper is well organized and clearly written. The literature review is extensive and up-to-date, providing a solid foundation for the proposed framework. The discussion of sector-specific challenges and technological pathways offers valuable insights into future industrial decarbonization strategies.
    Some minor improvements could further strengthen the manuscript:

    Include a schematic illustration of the proposed framework to improve visual communication.
    Further elaborate on potential implementation pathways for industrial adoption.
    Expand the discussion of economic and operational benefits associated with the proposed approach.
    Review minor formatting inconsistencies throughout the manuscript.

Overall, the paper presents a valuable and interesting contribution that highlights practical pathways for improving industrial resilience, reducing carbon emissions, and enhancing international competitiveness under future carbon regulatory frameworks.
10. Additional Confidential Comments to the Scientific Committee
The manuscript addresses a topic of considerable current interest and relevance to the conference themes. The work is well structured, supported by recent literature, and presents a coherent framework for integrating renewable energy, green hydrogen, energy storage, and digital monitoring in industrial supply chains. Although primarily conceptual in nature, the paper provides useful insights and identifies promising research and implementation directions. The overall quality of the manuscript is good, and it should be of interest to conference participants working in the fields of energy transition, sustainable manufacturing, and industrial decarbonization.
Proposal
Accept

contribution.title: Optimizing Baja SAE Suspensions: A Kinematic and Structural Study

revisions.judgment_comment:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer A:
This work presents an interesting study on the design and optimization of suspension and steering systems for a Baja SAE vehicle. The integrated use of kinematic analysis and finite element simulation provides a coherent engineering approach, and the reported results demonstrate the proposed design's potential. The manuscript is generally well structured and clearly describes the main design and simulation procedures. The authors appropriately acknowledge the virtual nature of the validation, identifying experimental track validation as future work. The conditions and definition of the Finite Element Model need a clearer description. The manuscript generally follows the conference template; however, the final version should be checked. Figure legends need minor formatting and presentation improvements.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer B:
The manuscript addresses a relevant Baja SAE suspension-design problem and presents an integrated kinematic and structural simulation approach. However, several issues should be addressed before acceptance. (i) The term “optimisation” is not sufficiently supported by the methodology. The authors should define the design variables, objective functions, constraints, initial configuration and criteria used to select the final hardpoint geometry. At present, the process appears mainly iterative. (ii) The statement that the selected roll-centre positions mitigate lateral load transfer should be revised. Roll-centre height affects the distribution between geometric and elastic load transfer and the roll moment, but does not directly reduce total lateral load transfer in the manner implied. (iii) Claims of superior tyre contact, enhanced lateral grip, predictable handling and eliminated bump steer should be moderated or supported by quantitative tyre, handling or experimental validation. (iv) The structural methodology requires more detail. The aluminium alloy designation, complete material properties, mesh size, convergence study, element formulation, boundary conditions and justification of the 4500 N landing load should be provided. (v) The abstract refers to structural evaluation of suspension arms and steering linkages, whereas the reported FEA focuses only on the steering knuckle. This inconsistency should be corrected. (vi) The claimed reduction in unsprung mass should be quantified against a reference design. (vii) The figures require substantial improvement. Several plots are low-resolution, contain Portuguese labels and have inconsistent graphical styles. Vector graphics should be used where possible. (viii) Citation placeholders such as “[cite: 2]” and “[cite: 1]” must be removed or corrected. (ix) The literature review is very limited and should better position the work against previous Baja SAE suspension studies. (x) The English should be revised for consistent UK English and scientific style. Major revision is recommended.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Editor:

[To be corrected]

The authors are requested to address all necessary corrections identified during the review process and resubmit the revised manuscript by 21 September 2026, 23:59 (Lisbon local time).
For manuscripts prepared using Microsoft Word, the authors must also submit a ZIP file containing all figures as separate files, numbered according to their appearance in the manuscript (e.g., fig01.png, fig02.svg, fig03.png). The figures should be provided in high quality, preferably in vector format (SVG) whenever applicable.

Thank you for the opportunity to revise the manuscript. I hope these changes address the main concerns raised.

Development and Preliminary Validation of a MATLAB Application for Plantar Thermal Asymmetry Detection in Diabetic Foot Assessment.pdf

revisions.judgment_comment:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer A:
The paper presents a relevant and technically interesting MATLAB-based application for semi-automated plantar thermographic analysis. The integration of plantar segmentation, ROI definition, contralateral mirroring, and thermal asymmetry detection provides a promising proof of concept. The comparison with HIKMICRO Analyzer is also useful as a preliminary assessment. However, several methodological issues should be addressed: i) The 42 paired measurements come from only 6 participants and therefore cannot be considered fully independent. The repeated-measures structure should be taken into account, particularly in the Wilcoxon and Bland–Altman analyses. ii) The paper should clearly distinguish software/functional validation from clinical validation. The small sample of healthy volunteers and the artificially heated coin demonstrate the ability to detect induced thermal asymmetry, but do not establish clinical performance in diabetic foot assessment. iii) More details are needed regarding the image-processing pipeline, particularly segmentation thresholds, ROI definition, mirroring and normalization procedures, geometric fallback rules, and the handling of invalid 5×5 cells. iv) The rationale and clinical interpretation of the proposed thresholds should be clarified. The term “High Risk” should be used cautiously unless supported by clinical evidence. The 0.21 °C difference from the reference software should also be discussed in terms of practical significance and, ideally, confidence intervals or additional agreement measures. HIKMICRO Analyzer should be presented as a reference for comparison, rather than as ground truth. v) Reporting participant-level results, the amount of manual intervention, and the robustness of the method to foot positioning and environmental conditions would strengthen the manuscript. Information on software or code availability would also improve reproducibility. Overall, the work is promising as a technical proof of concept. Comments to the Scientific Committee
This paper manuscript addresses a relevant and timely topic and presents a technically interesting MATLAB-based tool for the semi-automated analysis of plantar thermal asymmetry. The proposed approach is clearly described at a general level, and the preliminary comparison with commercial reference software provides encouraging evidence of its technical feasibility.
However, the scientific evidence remains limited. The validation is based on only six healthy volunteers and an artificially induced thermal stimulus and therefore does not provide evidence of clinical validity or diagnostic performance in patients with diabetes. In addition, the analysis of 42 repeated measurements from only six participants raises concerns regarding the independence of the observations and should be reconsidered or more clearly justified. Some aspects of the image-processing methodology are also insufficiently detailed to ensure full reproducibility.
Nevertheless, the manuscript is transparent about its limitations and appropriately presents the results as preliminary. The work may be suitable for the conference as a proof-of-concept and technical contribution, particularly given its potential relevance to emerging biomedical engineering applications.
Acceptance would be more strongly supported if the authors clarify the statistical methodology, provide additional details to improve the reproducibility of the computational pipeline, and ensure that the conclusions consistently remain within the scope of preliminary technical validation rather than clinical validation.

contribution.title: Intelligent Fault Diagnosis in Boost Power Converters: A Systematic Literature Review

revisions.judgment_comment:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer A:
This paper addresses a very timely and important topic, exploring how artificial intelligence can be used to monitor the health of aluminum electrolytic capacitors in boost converters. The motivation behind the work is clear, the structure is well-organized, and the three research questions do a great job of framing the discussion. To help the authors enhance the impact of their work further, I would suggest considering the following issues: - It would be helpful to provide a bit more detail on how the literature was selected. Sharing details like the databases searched, keywords used, timeframe, inclusion / exclusion criteria, and the total number of papers analyzed would greatly strengthen this section. - Including a structured comparative table of the reviewed studies would provide an excellent overview for the reader. However, I completely understand if space constraints—given the 5-page limit—might make this difficult to include. - When comparing Machine Learning and Deep Learning methods, adding a bit more nuance and, if available, some quantitative evidence would make those comparisons even more compelling. - It might be beneficial to slightly moderate some of the broader assertions so that the final conclusions align better with the specific evidence presented in the study.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer B:
Please consider the following reviewer concerns: 1 The literature-review methodology should be described, including the databases, search terms, publication period, selection criteria, and number of studies identified and included. 2 A synthesis table should compare the selected studies in terms of converter topology, diagnosed component, input signals, extracted features, AI method, dataset, validation procedure, and main results. 3 The stated focus on boost converters and aluminum electrolytic capacitors is not consistently maintained, since several cited studies concern motors, smart grids, microgrids, or other application areas. 4 Claims that CNNs outperform SVMs and Random Forests, or that particular models are the most effective, require direct comparative evidence from the reviewed studies and should otherwise be moderated. 5 Please expand and verify the bibliography, prioritizing primary studies on capacitor fault diagnosis in boost converters, correct the incomplete reference [11], and revise the formatting, including the irregular spacing and “X” page footers. Thank you.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Editor:

[To be corrected]

The authors are requested to address all necessary corrections identified during the review process and resubmit the revised manuscript by 21 September 2026, 23:59 (Lisbon local time).
For manuscripts prepared using Microsoft Word, the authors must also submit a ZIP file containing all figures as separate files, numbered according to their appearance in the manuscript (e.g., fig01.png, fig02.svg, fig03.png). The figures should be provided in high quality, preferably in vector format (SVG) whenever applicable.

ratings.value:
This paper addresses a very timely and important topic, exploring how artificial intelligence can be used to monitor the health of aluminum electrolytic capacitors in boost converters. The motivation behind the work is clear, the structure is well-organized, and the three research questions do a great job of framing the discussion. To help the authors enhance the impact of their work further, I would suggest considering the following issues:

- It would be helpful to provide a bit more detail on how the literature was selected. Sharing details like the databases searched, keywords used, timeframe, inclusion / exclusion criteria, and the total number of papers analyzed would greatly strengthen this section.

- Including a structured comparative table of the reviewed studies would provide an excellent overview for the reader. However, I completely understand if space constraints—given the 5-page limit—might make this difficult to include.

- When comparing Machine Learning and Deep Learning methods, adding a bit more nuance and, if available, some quantitative evidence would make those comparisons even more compelling.

- It might be beneficial to slightly moderate some of the broader assertions so that the final conclusions align better with the specific evidence presented in the study.

contribution.title: Comparative Analysis of Pope and GRI-Mech Mechanisms for Methane Using the Cantera Library

revisions.judgment_comment:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer A:
The paper presents a clear and relevant comparative study of the detailed GRI-Mech 3.0 and the reduced Pope-based mechanism, using consistent numerical and operating conditions within the Cantera framework. The results are particularly convincing in demonstrating the substantial computational benefit of the reduced mechanism, with a 70.7% reduction in CPU time while maintaining very close agreement in key global combustion characteristics, including adiabatic flame temperature. Overall, the paper provides a useful and practically relevant contribution to computational combustion modelling by demonstrating a good balance between chemical-model simplification, computational efficiency, and preservation of the main physical characteristics of methane flames.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Editor:


[Accepted]
The paper has been accepted for publication.

revisions.judgment_comment:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer A:
This paper presents a techno-economic feasibility analysis of green hydrogen production via water electrolysis, focusing on a 10 MW Proton Exchange Membrane (PEM) electrolyser in the Portuguese energy context. The topic is relevant, the methodology is appropriate, and the results are of interest for researchers and practitioners working on green hydrogen. I would like to suggest some issues that may improve the quality of the paper: - The terms “competitive,” “economically viable,” and “ideal technical-economic trade-off,” would work better if the authors provide a benchmark (e.g., comparison with grey/blue hydrogen costs) - The manuscript uses “load factor” to describe the annual operating intensity of the electrolyser. I believe the term “capacity factor” is more suitable. - Consider adding a short sentence explicitly stating that the 0.22 €/kg corresponds to the 8-day case in Table 3. - The manuscript alternates between “AEL” and “AWE” for alkaline water electrolysis. Please choose one abbreviation and use it consistently.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer B:
The paper presents a relevant techno-economic assessment of a 10 MW PEM green hydrogen production system in the Portuguese context. The sensitivity analyses provide useful insight into the influence of load factor, electricity price, and hydrogen storage on LCOH. A few minor revisions would improve the precision and presentation of the manuscript. (i) The conclusion that a 4-8 day hydrogen reserve represents an "ideal" technical-economic trade-off should be moderated or further justified. The study quantifies the additional storage cost, but does not quantitatively evaluate supply-security benefits, delivery reliability, or alternative storage strategies. Expressions such as "massive surge in supply security" should therefore be replaced by more objective wording. Please also clarify how the assumed storage CAPEX and 30-year storage lifetime are treated within the 20-year project horizon. (ii) Figures 1-3 should be improved in quality and consistency with the manuscript. All text included in the figures should be in English and, where possible, use the same font as the manuscript, such as Computer Modern. The figures may be redrawn using Ipe, Inkscape, or another vector-graphics tool. Where figures are reproduced or adapted from references, the source and any required permissions should be clearly indicated. Preferably, figures should be supplied as SVG or another vector format, or as high-resolution PNG/TIFF files. (iii) Please revise the author and affiliation information according to the conference and institutional naming conventions. The telephone number should be removed, the institutional affiliation should be presented consistently, and only one email address, preferably that of the corresponding author, should be provided.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Editor:

[To be corrected]

The authors are requested to address all necessary corrections identified during the review process and resubmit the revised manuscript by 21 September 2026, 23:59 (Lisbon local time).
For manuscripts prepared using Microsoft Word, the authors must also submit a ZIP file containing all figures as separate files, numbered according to their appearance in the manuscript (e.g., fig01.png, fig02.svg, fig03.png). The figures should be provided in high quality, preferably in vector format (SVG) whenever applicable.

revisions.judgment_comment:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer A:
Please give a detailed explanation about the buildings consedered. Architecture, insulation, glazing, location, solar radiation, usage are factors which significantly influence the results. The effects of these must be clearly described and evaluated. The buildings should be presented with sketches so that we can imagine them.

revisions.judgment_comment:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer A:
The manuscript addresses a timely and relevant topic: the design of electrical infrastructure for data centers, combining availability, redundancy, energy efficiency, and photovoltaic integration. Its strengths include its practical orientation, the discussion of critical loads, UPS systems, emergency generators, reactive-power compensation, and PV self-consumption, as well as the clear presentation of N, N+1, 2N, and 2(N+1) redundancy schemes and operating modes. Suggestions for improvement: The paper includes a quantitative application to a Class 2 data center. A short dedicated case-study section could improve the manuscript by clearly identifying the assumptions, input data, simulation procedure, and main outcomes. Information on site conditions, PV orientation and tilt, equipment specifications, losses, simulation tool, and optimization criterion would be particularly useful. However, the page limit may restrict the extent to which this suggestion can be implemented. An annual PV generation of 1,822 MWh represents approximately 27.7% of an annual consumption of 6.57 GWh, rather than the reported 26.1%. This may result from rounding, a typographical error, or a distinction between gross PV generation and self-consumed energy, but it should be clarified. The conclusion refers to a “technical and economic balance,” although no economic analysis is clearly presented. This statement should therefore be supported by a brief economic assessment or rephrased to reflect only the technical and environmental aspects assessed in the paper.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The authors should also improve the graphical quality and legibility of the figures, author information and order and formatting of the references. Subject to the satisfactory completion of these revisions, the manuscript may be accepted for presentation at the conference.

contribution.title: Environmental Anonymous Noise-Based In-Situ Sound Absorption Characterization Using Standard Laboratory Assets

revisions.judgment_comment:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer A:
The paper presents an interesting and practically relevant approach for in-situ acoustic characterization using standard laboratory equipment. However, several aspects should be clarified before acceptance. (i) The reference absorption data used for validation must be fully identified and cited. Please clarify whether the reference conditions, sample properties, mounting, and backing are directly comparable with the present experiments. If full comparability cannot be established, the term "validation" should be moderated. (ii) Please provide the mathematical definitions of MPE and MAPE and explain how octave-band values are aggregated. (iii) Since excluding the 125 Hz and 250 Hz bands substantially improves the reported errors, an objective and reproducible exclusion criterion should be defined, preferably based on coherence or another pre-established validity condition. (iv) The statement that underestimation is evidenced by equivalence between MPE and MAPE should be revised, since this does not hold for all cases. (v) Claims relating improved performance to temporal energy density and spectral entropy should be quantitatively supported or presented more cautiously. (vi) Please clarify the distinction between microphone spacing l and surface distance d, and support the corresponding parametric conclusions with the relevant results. (vii) Measurement repeatability or uncertainty should be reported from the repeated acquisitions. (viii) Figures 1-4 should be substantially improved in resolution, readability, and consistency. Preferably, use vector graphics prepared with TikZ/LaTeX, Inkscape, Ipe, or another suitable graphical tool, supplied as SVG or equivalent vector format, using Computer Modern where possible. (ix) The references require careful verification. Reference [2] contains an incorrect issue number, Reference [3] contains substantial bibliographic inconsistencies, and Reference [4] should be updated to ISO 10534-2:2023 unless use of the 1998 edition is specifically justified. Please verify all entries against the original sources and include DOIs where available.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer B:
This research proposes an alternative method for characterizing sound-absorption materials that avoids high-cost commercial equipment. The authors developed an in-situ methodology using general-purpose lab equipment and tested the setup with rock and glass wool under four scenarios. The results show high metrological errors, particularly in specific frequency bands, but the authors identify several limitations to be overcome in future developments of the experimental setup.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Editor:

[To be corrected]

The authors are requested to address all necessary corrections identified during the review process and resubmit the revised manuscript by 21 September 2026, 23:59 (Lisbon local time).
For manuscripts prepared using Microsoft Word, the authors must also submit a ZIP file containing all figures as separate files, numbered according to their appearance in the manuscript (e.g., fig01.png, fig02.svg, fig03.png). The figures should be provided in high quality, preferably in vector format (SVG) whenever applicable.

revisions.judgment_comment:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer A:
The paper is well structured and the results are relevant for condition monitoring of rotating machinery. The limitations of the experimental study are also clearly stated. Overall, I consider the paper suitable for presentation at the conference and recommend its acceptance.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer B:
The paper presents a timely and relevant experimental approach to investigating electrical discharge damage in rolling bearings, combining controlled current loading with bidirectional vibration monitoring and multiple signal-processing techniques. The experimental results provide valuable evidence of progressive bearing degradation, with complementary information from the horizontal and vertical vibration measurements and clear increases in vibration indicators over the investigated period. Overall, the paper makes a promising contribution toward the development of reproducible RUL prognostic testing for electrically stressed bearings, and the proposed extension toward synchronized electrical, vibration, and mechanical measurements provides a strong basis for future research.

contribution.title: Regulatory and Implementation Framework for Renewable Energy Communities in Portugal

revisions.judgment_comment:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer A:
The manuscript addresses a relevant topic. However, several issues should be resolved before acceptance. (i) The temporal scope of the dataset is inconsistent: the methodology refers to July 2026, whereas the results repeatedly describe an annual energy balance. The analysed period and temporal resolution should therefore be clarified throughout the manuscript. (ii) The energy balance and performance indicators require correction. The 36.03 MWh are described as energy made available to the REC, yet Table 2 labels this quantity as exported energy, and the reported export rate of 87.71% is inconsistent with the definition provided. (iii) The residual difference of approximately 0.24 MWh should be explicitly included and treated consistently, and all percentages should be recalculated using clearly defined reference values. (iv) The abstract refers to a comparative analysis involving selected European countries, but such analysis is not developed in the manuscript; it should either be added or removed. (v) The quantitative methodology should be made reproducible by specifying the number of records, actual sampling resolution, treatment of missing data (preprocessing) and validation criteria. (vi) The legal nature of the analysed project should be clarified, since the manuscript alternates between collective self-consumption and a Renewable Energy Community despite distinguishing these concepts legally. (vii) The figures should be improved in quality and clarity, preferably using vector formats such as SVG or PNG with high qualit where possible. The stakeholder framework figure should be corrected, as it appears to show two arrows at the extremes instead of a single clear directional flow. In Figure 2, the legend should be removed from inside the figure and the relevant information transferred to the caption or main text. (viii) The references should be revised, particularly the legal sources. (ix) The English must be revised (UK).
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer B:
The manuscript addresses a timely and relevant topic by combining an analysis of the Portuguese regulatory framework for Renewable Energy Communities with a practical implementation workflow and operational case study. Its principal strengths are the connection between regulation and practice, the use of measured energy data, and the participant-level assessment of energy sharing. However, the authors must carry out the following revisions: - Review the formatting and number the equations in the text. - Format and complete the information associated with the references. Standardise the references, cite legislation by its complete official designation, consolidate duplicated DGEG sources, and remove utm_source=chatgpt.com from the URLs. - Improve the dimensions and legibility of Figures 1, 2 e 3. - Specify the exact monitoring period and temporal resolution. The manuscript refers to July 2026 but subsequently describes the results as an “annual energy balance.” - Review the text formatting; some text is in bold. The paper provides useful practical insights for improving local renewable-energy utilisation and supports acceptance for presentation at the conference, subject to appropriate revisions.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Editor:

[To be corrected]

The authors are requested to address all necessary corrections identified during the review process and resubmit the revised manuscript by 21 September 2026, 23:59 (Lisbon local time).
For manuscripts prepared using Microsoft Word, the authors must also submit a ZIP file containing all figures as separate files, numbered according to their appearance in the manuscript (e.g., fig01.png, fig02.svg, fig03.png). The figures should be provided in high quality, preferably in vector format (SVG) whenever applicable.

ratings.value:
The manuscript addresses a timely and relevant topic by combining an analysis of the Portuguese regulatory framework for Renewable Energy Communities with a practical implementation workflow and operational case study. Its principal strengths are the connection between regulation and practice, the use of measured energy data, and the participant-level assessment of energy sharing.
However, the authors must carry out the following revisions:
-	Review the formatting and number the equations in the text.
-	Format and complete the information associated with the references. Standardise the references, cite legislation by its complete official designation, consolidate duplicated DGEG sources, and remove utm_source=chatgpt.com from the URLs.
-	Improve the dimensions and legibility of Figures 1, 2 e 3.
-	Specify the exact monitoring period and temporal resolution. The manuscript refers to July 2026 but subsequently describes the results as an “annual energy balance.”
-	Review the text formatting; some text is in bold.
The paper provides useful practical insights for improving local renewable-energy utilisation and supports acceptance for presentation at the conference, subject to appropriate revisions.

ratings.value:
The manuscript addresses a relevant topic. However, several issues should be resolved before acceptance. (i) The temporal scope of the dataset is inconsistent: the methodology refers to July 2026, whereas the results repeatedly describe an annual energy balance. The analysed period and temporal resolution should therefore be clarified throughout the manuscript.
(ii) The energy balance and performance indicators require correction. The 36.03 MWh are described as energy made available to the REC, yet Table 2 labels this quantity as exported energy, and the reported export rate of 87.71% is inconsistent with the definition provided.
(iii) The residual difference of approximately 0.24 MWh should be explicitly included and treated consistently, and all percentages should be recalculated using clearly defined reference values.
(iv) The abstract refers to a comparative analysis involving selected European countries, but such analysis is not developed in the manuscript; it should either be added or removed.
(v) The quantitative methodology should be made reproducible by specifying the number of records, actual sampling resolution, treatment of missing data (preprocessing) and validation criteria.
(vi) The legal nature of the analysed project should be clarified, since the manuscript alternates between collective self-consumption and a Renewable Energy Community despite distinguishing these concepts legally.
(vii) The figures should be improved in quality and clarity, preferably using vector formats such as SVG or PNG with high qualit where possible. The stakeholder framework figure should be corrected, as it appears to show two arrows at the extremes instead of a single clear directional flow. In Figure 2, the legend should be removed from inside the figure and the relevant information transferred to the caption or main text. (viii) The references should be revised, particularly the legal sources. (ix) The English must be revised (UK).

comments.html:
Dear reviewers, thank you for your assessment of the submitted paper. I believe all the concerns raised have been addressed, though I would like to express two concerns. (i) Unfortunately, the changes necessary to accommodate some of the points addressed mean that information which had been previously cut in order to respect the 5 page limit, now had to be included. This resulted in a 7 page document, though one and a half are references and acknowledgements. (ii) Upon reviewing the sources, I noticed some of the biomass properties used were inaccurate, as a result of additional experimentation, and felt it appropriate to run the model an additional time. As a result some of the values are slightly different, both in the inputs and the results, though the differences are quite small.

Best regards,
Frederico Kossack

revisions.judgment_comment:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer A:
The analytical model for the transportable autothermal biochar reactor is well-structured and thermodynamically sound. For the final version, report the feedstock analysis (Pinus pinaster), clarify the units in Eq. 22, and replace lecture-slide citations with peer-reviewed references. Lastly, provide the main geometric dimensions of the reactor body and screw conveyor to ensure reproducibility.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Reviewer B:
The paper presents a relevant and technically interesting concept for a transportable continuous biochar reactor supported by an analytical model. The contribution is suitable for the conference, but several revisions are recommended to improve reproducibility, presentation, and scientific rigour. (i) Please use consistent terminology, particularly "autothermal" versus "autothermic". (ii) The Abstract should be rewritten and expanded to provide a more representative summary of the actual work, including the modelling approach, main assumptions, principal parameters evaluated, key quantitative results, and main limitations. (iii) Please provide a compact table summarising the principal model inputs, assumptions, biomass properties, operating conditions, and geometric parameters. (iv) The applicability of the heat-transfer correlations should be supported by the corresponding Reynolds, Rayleigh, and Prandtl numbers. The convergence criterion used in the iterative determination of biomass combustion should also be stated explicitly. (v) Equation (22) should be reformatted so that its numbering and alignment are consistent with the remaining equations. Chemical formulae and species should preferably be typeset using the "mhchem" package available from CTAN, while physical quantities and units should be formatted consistently using "siunitx". (vi) Section 3 should contain a short introductory paragraph before Section 3.1 explaining the scope and organisation of the results. (vii) The figures should be substantially improved. Where possible, use vector graphics with a font consistent with the manuscript, preferably Computer Modern. TikZ/LaTeX, Ipe, Inkscape, or another vector-graphics tool may be used. (viii) Please strengthen the references supporting the modelling assumptions and empirical correlations by prioritising peer-reviewed scientific literature instead of lecture slides or teaching material. (ix) The affiliation should be written in English and formatted consistently. Only one corresponding-author email address should be provided. (x) Keywords should be reduced to five, lowercase, and alphabetically ordered: analytical modeling; autothermal reactor; biochar; biomass valorization; continuous pyrolysis.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Assess the clarity, coherence and logical organisation of the manuscript, including the precision of the scientific and technical terminology, the quality and appropriateness of figures, tables and equations, and the correct and relevant use of scientific literature and references.

Rating scale:
1 — Poor: The criterion is not satisfactorily met; fundamental deficiencies are present.
2 — Weak: Substantial deficiencies are present and significant improvement is required.
3 — Adequate: The criterion is met at an acceptable level, although relevant improvements are required.
4 — Good: The criterion is well addressed, with only limited weaknesses.
5 — Excellent: The criterion is addressed to a high scientific and technical standard.

ratings.value:
The analytical model for the transportable autothermal biochar reactor is well-structured and thermodynamically sound.
For the final version, report the feedstock analysis (Pinus pinaster), clarify the units in Eq. 22, and replace lecture-slide citations with peer-reviewed references.
Lastly, provide the main geometric dimensions of the reactor body and screw conveyor to ensure reproducibility.
